claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
Repeated arc melting produces a refined nanoscale heterogeneous microstructure in WTaTiVZr.
The proposed heterogeneous microstructure includes a dispersion of fine secondary phases.
Repeated arc melting modifies the grain boundaries of WTaTiVZr.
Microstructural refinement enhances dislocation mobility at elevated temperatures.
Microstructural refinement promotes grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperatures.
The arc-melted equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a fine and compositionally complex microstructure.
The arc-melted WTaTiVZr alloy has a multiphase microstructure.
Temperatures approaching or exceeding 1000 degrees Celsius under sustained loading are representative of plasma-facing-component service.
The nanoscale heterogeneities arise from both the equimolar alloy composition and repeated remelting.
The refined microstructure facilitates dislocation nucleation.
Enhanced dislocation nucleation and mobility improve high-temperature plastic deformation and toughness.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding improves high-temperature plastic deformation and toughness.
Under high-temperature mechanical testing, WTaTiVZr is expected to absorb more energy before failure than pure tungsten.
The predicted advantage depends on retention of the refined microstructure.
Microstructural coarsening may eliminate the predicted performance advantage.
Temperatures or strain rates outside the proposed service regime may activate alternative deformation mechanisms and eliminate the predicted advantage.

contradictions.description: The tungsten comparator is inconsistently specified as conventionally processed or standard tungsten in some fields but as tungsten processed under conditions analogous to repeated arc melting in the experiment. Thus, the intended processing-matched control is ambiguous.
